Theme

Nature & food

grove noun

also wood (a small one), copse, woodland, sacred grove, spinney, plantation

classical

Cic. Div. 1.114: multōs nemora silvaeque commovent (Lewis & Short)
Hor. C. 3.22.1: montium custōs nemorumque (Lewis & Short)
Ov. F. 6.9: nemus arboribus dēnsum (Lewis & Short)

nemus, nemoris n.

noun, third declension

a wood with open glades; a grove

A wood with open places and pasture in it, where silva is the wild, unbroken forest; in the poets any wood (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • lūcus, lūcī m. — a sacred grove

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Mil. 85: vōs jam, Albānī tumulī atque lūcī, implōrō (Lewis & Short); Liv. 24.3: lūcus frequentī silvā saeptus (Lewis & Short)

    A stand of trees sacred to a god. Servius’s distinction: lūcus is trees with religious awe, nemus an ordered stand of trees, silva spreading and wild (Lewis & Short).

  • arbustum, arbustī n. — a plantation of trees; in the poets (plural) trees, a copse

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cato Agr. 1.7 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Sen. 54 (Lewis & Short); Verg. G. 2.416: jam falcem arbusta repōnunt (Lewis & Short)

    In farming, a plantation, above all one of trees on which vines are trained.

Examples

  • tē nemus omne canet

    every grove will sing of youVerg. E. 6.11

  • sōle sub ardentī resonant arbusta cicādīs

    under the burning sun the trees ring with cicadasVerg. E. 2.13

See also forest, glade, tree, undergrowth, orchard.

SourcesLewis & Short: nemus · Lewis & Short: lucus · Lewis & Short: arbustum

Vergil, Eclogae 6.11, 2.13.
